lessonTitle: Carnot Refrigerators and Heat Pumps: Limits of Cooling Performance

blocks.text: A hospital vaccine fridge holds 4 C inside a ward at 24 C. Its compressor must keep pumping heat uphill from the cold box to the warm room, and the thermodynamic minimum cost of that pumping can be calculated from the two temperatures alone.

blocks.markdown: A **refrigerator** is a cycle that removes heat $Q_L$ from a cold space and rejects heat $Q_H$ to a warm environment by consuming work $W_{in}$. A **heat pump** is the same device used to deliver $Q_H$ to a warm space. The performance measure is not an efficiency but a **coefficient of performance (COP)**: desired effect divided by the work paid for.

blocks.caption: Energy balance for a cycle: Q_H = Q_L + W_in

blocks.markdown: The best possible refrigerator runs the Carnot cycle in reverse, taking heat from the cold space at $T_L$ and rejecting it at $T_H$, with every process reversible. Using $Q_L/Q_H=T_L/T_H$ for a reversible cycle (a result of the second law) gives the upper bound:

blocks.caption: Temperatures in kelvin; the cold space is at T_L and the environment at T_H

blocks.title: Temperature lift controls COP
blocks.text: The Carnot COP depends on the temperature lift $T_H-T_L$. A small lift (a cool drink cabinet in a mild room) gives a high COP; a large lift (a deep freezer in a hot kitchen) gives a low COP. COP can exceed 1 because the work only moves heat rather than creating it.

blocks.title: Chest freezer at -18 C
blocks.prompt: A freezer holds -18 C in a room at 30 C and must remove 2.4 kW of heat. Find the maximum COP and the minimum compressor power. A real unit with COP 2.2 is tested; how good is it?

steps.text: Convert to kelvin: $T_L=255.15$ K, $T_H=303.15$ K. Maximum COP.
Minimum power for a 2.4 kW load.
Compare the real COP to the limit.

blocks.answer: COP_max = 5.32, minimum power 451 W; the real unit reaches 41 % of the Carnot limit.

blocks.markdown: To **judge the quality** of a real machine, compare its COP with the Carnot COP between the same temperatures. The ratio $\mathrm{COP}_{real}/\mathrm{COP}_{max}$, sometimes called the second-law efficiency, is always less than 1. Typical domestic machines reach perhaps 20 to 50 % of the limit; a ratio close to or above 1 means the data are wrong or the reservoirs have been misidentified.

blocks.title: Warm-room cooling versus heating
blocks.prompt: A space at -5 C is cooled by rejecting heat to surroundings at 22 C. Compute the Carnot COP as a refrigerator. What would the COP be if the same reversible device delivered heat at 22 C as a heat pump?

steps.text: Convert to kelvin: $T_L=268.15$ K and $T_H=295.15$ K.
Heat pump COP from the relation.

items: Convert both temperatures to kelvin before any ratio.
Identify which space is cold ($T_L$) and which is the environment ($T_H$).
Compute the Carnot COP; use it to find the minimum work for a given heat load.
Divide the real COP by the Carnot COP to judge performance.

blocks.title: Heat flow is not work
blocks.text: A COP of 4 does not mean 400 % efficiency. It means 4 kJ of heat is moved for each kJ of work. The work cannot be reduced below $Q_L/\mathrm{COP}_{max}$.

blocks.title: State the temperatures
blocks.text: Say which temperature is which and show the kelvin conversion. A common error is putting the Celsius values into the COP formula.

points: COP of a refrigerator is Q_L divided by work input and, for a heat pump, Q_H divided by work input.
The Carnot refrigerator COP is T_L/(T_H - T_L) with absolute temperatures; it is the upper bound.
The minimum work for a heat load Q_L is Q_L divided by the Carnot COP.
Real quality is judged by COP_real / COP_Carnot, which must be below 1.

questions.stem: Which expression gives the maximum COP of a refrigerator keeping a cold space at T_L in surroundings at T_H (absolute temperatures)?

options.text: T_H / (T_H - T_L)
1 - T_L / T_H
T_L / (T_H - T_L)
(T_H - T_L) / T_L

distractorRationale.a: That is the heat pump limit.
distractorRationale.b: That is the Carnot engine efficiency.

questions.explanation: The reversible refrigerator removes Q_L at T_L and rejects Q_H at T_H, with Q_L/Q_H = T_L/T_H. Substituting into COP = Q_L/(Q_H - Q_L) gives T_L/(T_H - T_L).

questions.stem: For a refrigerator removing a heat load Q_L from a cold space, what is the least work that must be supplied?

options.text: Q_L divided by the Carnot COP
Q_L multiplied by the Carnot COP
Zero, since the heat flow is free
Q_L itself

questions.correctOptionText: Q_L divided by the Carnot COP

distractorRationale.d: That would give a COP of 1.

questions.explanation: COP is Q_L over W, so W = Q_L/COP, and the work is smallest when the COP is largest, i.e. the Carnot value. Any real machine needs more work than this.

questions.stem: A display cabinet keeps 2 C inside a shop at 22 C. If the shop warms to 32 C with the same cabinet temperature, what happens to the Carnot COP?

options.text: It increases because the surroundings are warmer
It decreases because the temperature lift increases
It stays the same because T_L is unchanged
It becomes infinite

questions.correctOptionText: It decreases because the temperature lift increases

distractorRationale.a: A larger lift decreases the COP.
distractorRationale.c: The COP depends on T_H - T_L too.
distractorRationale.d: It would be infinite only when T_H = T_L.

questions.explanation: The Carnot COP is T_L/(T_H - T_L). T_L stays at 275.15 K, but T_H - T_L rises from 20 K to 30 K, so the COP falls from about 13.8 to 9.2.

questions.stem: A manufacturer claims a freezer at -20 C in a 25 C room has a COP of 7. Between these temperatures the Carnot COP is about 5.6. How should the claim be judged?

options.text: Plausible, since COP can exceed 1
Plausible if the compressor is large
Impossible because COP must be below 1
Impossible, since it exceeds the Carnot limit

questions.correctOptionText: Impossible, since it exceeds the Carnot limit

distractorRationale.a: COP above 1 is fine, but not above the Carnot limit.
distractorRationale.c: COP can exceed 1, just not the reversible limit.

questions.explanation: The Carnot COP of 253.15/45 = 5.6 is the ceiling, so a COP of 7 would violate the second law. COP above 1 is normal but must stay below that limit.

questions.stem: Two refrigerators reject heat to the same 30 C ambient. One holds a cabinet at 5 C and the other a freezer at -20 C. Both have a real COP of 3.0. Which statement about quality relative to the Carnot limit is correct?

options.text: Both are equally good because their COPs are equal
The freezer is the better machine because its Carnot limit is lower, so 3.0 is a larger fraction of it
The cabinet unit is the better machine because its limit is lower
Neither can be compared with a Carnot cycle

questions.correctOptionText: The freezer is the better machine because its Carnot limit is lower, so 3.0 is a larger fraction of it

distractorRationale.a: Equal COPs do not mean equal quality: the limits differ.

questions.explanation: The Carnot COP is 278.15/25 = 11.1 for the cabinet and 253.15/50 = 5.1 for the freezer. A COP of 3.0 is only 27 % of the former limit but 59 % of the latter, so the freezer machine performs better relative to its limit.

questions.stem: A refrigerator keeps a cold space at 5 C in surroundings at 35 C. Find the maximum possible COP (use T(K) = T(C) + 273.15; dimensionless).
questions.explanation: The temperatures are 278.15 K and 308.15 K, so COP_max = 278.15/30 = 9.272. This is the ceiling for any refrigerator between these temperatures.

questions.stem: A cold store must remove 5 kW of heat at -10 C while rejecting heat to surroundings at 25 C. Find the minimum compressor power in kW.
questions.explanation: The Carnot COP is 263.15/35 = 7.519, so the minimum power is 5/7.519 = 0.665 kW. A real compressor draws more.

questions.stem: A refrigerator removes 3.0 kW from a space at -5 C and draws 1.5 kW of electrical power while rejecting heat to 30 C surroundings. What percentage of the Carnot COP does it achieve?
questions.explanation: Its COP is 3.0/1.5 = 2.0, while the Carnot COP is 268.15/35 = 7.661. The ratio is 2.0/7.661 = 26.1 %, a modest quality typical of small machines.

questions.stem: Explain why the maximum COP of a refrigerator rises as the temperature of the cold space is raised, with the ambient fixed. Then say why a COP greater than 1 does not violate energy conservation.
markingGuide: Raising T_L increases the numerator and reduces the temperature lift T_H - T_L
So COP rises and the minimum work for a given Q_L falls
A refrigerator moves heat Q_L from the cold space rather than converting work into heat
Energy balance Q_H = Q_L + W_in is satisfied, and COP = Q_L/W_in can exceed 1
questions.explanation: A smaller temperature lift means less work is needed to lift each joule of heat. The COP exceeds 1 because the work only moves energy, so the energy balance Q_H = Q_L + W_in holds.

questions.stem: A refrigerator removes 2 kW from a cold room at 2 C and rejects heat to ambient at 32 C while drawing 0.6 kW. Compute the Carnot COP and the actual COP and use them to judge the machine, stating the minimum power the load could require.
markingGuide: Convert to kelvin: T_L = 275.15 K, T_H = 305.15 K
Ratio about 36 % of the limit, so the quality is moderate with room for improvement
Minimum power = 2/9.17 = 0.218 kW, well below the 0.6 kW actually drawn
questions.explanation: The Carnot COP sets the minimum power at about 0.22 kW, while the machine draws 0.6 kW, giving a COP of 3.3 against 9.2. The ratio of about 0.36 is a measure of how far the real cycle is from reversible.
